items.title: Sunny and mild Sunday ahead for Toronto, Mississauga and GTA
items.summary: While parts of northern Ontario brace for up to 20 cm of snow, residents across the GTA and Niagara can expect a sunny and unseasonably mild Sunday, according to Environment Canada. Tonight (Saturday, Nov. 21) will be clear across the region, with fog patches developing. Lows will be around 5 C in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington, and 7 C in Durham Region and Niagara. Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington will see a high of 14 C. Durham Region will be slightly warmer at 15 C, with south winds of 30 km/h and a mix of sun and cloud late in the afternoon. Niagara will be the warmest spot in the region, with a high of 16 C and south winds of 20 km/h. Clouds will roll in Sunday night, with a 30 per cent chance of showers overnight in most areas. Durham could see a few showers beginning near midnight. Winds will also pick up overnight, becoming northwest at 30 km/h with gusts up to 50 km/h in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington. In Durham and Niagara, winds will become northwest at 20 km/h, gusting to 40 km/h. Overnight lows will be 6 C in Toronto, 4 C in Mississauga, Brampton and Burlington, 3 C in Durham and 7 C in Niagara. Drivers should watch for fog early Sunday morning, which can reduce visibility on roads and highways.

items.title: Woman seriously injured in two-vehicle crash in Mississauga
items.summary: A woman has been taken to a trauma centre with serious injuries after a two-vehicle crash in Mississauga on Saturday afternoon. m. on Saturday (Nov. 21). A female driver was taken to a trauma centre with serious injuries, police said. A male driver was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries. Southbound Hurontario Street was closed from Eglinton Avenue to Elia Avenue while police investigated. Drivers were asked to use alternate routes. Police have not said what caused the crash or whether any charges are expected. Hurontario Street is one of Mississauga’s busiest roads, running north–south through the city, and the Eglinton intersection is one of its main crossings. Anyone with information or dashcam footage is asked to contact Peel police and quote occurrence number PR260394750, or contact Crime Stoppers anonymously at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477). items.title: Mississauga collision sends two drivers to hospital
items.summary: Two drivers have been injured in a two-vehicle collision in Mississauga. m. for the collision in the area of Eglinton Avenue West and Hurontario Street. A female driver was transported to a trauma centre with serious injuries, while a male driver was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries, police say. The cause of the collision is not immediately known. Police say there are road closures in the area for the investigation.

items.title: Mississauga Arts Council Honours Billy Talent for 15 Years Backing Mental Health Charity Make Music Matter
items.summary: According to CBC Peel, the Mississauga Arts Council presented Billy Talent with an award this week recognizing the punk rock band's work beyond its music career. The council says the honour reflects the band's long-running support for Make Music Matter, a mental health charity the group has backed for 15 years. CBC Peel reports the charity uses songwriting as a therapeutic tool meant to empower and help heal people. Host Nav Nanwa covered the recognition for CBC Peel. The award highlights local artists whose community contributions extend past their creative output, according to the broadcaster.

items.title: Church Street Reopens After Vehicle Strikes and Seriously Injures Pedestrian in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Peel police, a pedestrian was seriously injured after being struck by a vehicle in Mississauga. Police say the pedestrian was taken to a local hospital with serious injuries following the collision. The driver remained at the scene after the crash, according to police. Officers temporarily closed Church Street between Old Pine Street and Main Street while emergency crews responded to the scene. Police say the intersection has since reopened to traffic. No further details about the pedestrian's condition were immediately available.

items.title: Car Insurance ON Mississauga
items.summary: In 2026, the average car insurance premium in Mississauga is $3,078 per year (about $257 per month). 01% higher than the provincial average of $2,653. This makes Mississauga 176th out of 181 Ontario communities for car insurance affordability. As of July 1, 2026 in Ontario, some previously mandatory accident benefits are now optional. ca data, drivers in Mississauga pay about $3,078 per year for auto insurance as of March 2026. Drivers here pay premiums that are higher than in Burlington, which is the cheapest city for car insurance in the GTA at $2,109 per year. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. Nearby Oakville has an average premium of $2,167 per year ($181 per month), which is $911 less than Mississauga. Car insurance premiums depend on many factors, such as the number of claims in an area, the amount of time drivers spend on the road, and each driver’s personal and insurance history. The lowest average premium in Mississauga is found in the L5J area, where drivers pay $2,737 annually. Meanwhile, drivers in L4T have the highest average premiums at $3,937 per year.

items.title: Mississauga Man Faces New Charges in Human Trafficking Investigation
items.summary: A 36-year-old Mississauga man has been charged with additional offences in a human-trafficking investigation and remains before the courts.

items.title: Officers Misjudged Jamal Francique's Walking Pace Before Arrest Turned Into Takedown, Inquest Told
items.summary: According to testimony at the coroner's inquest into the police shooting death of Jamal Francique, Peel Regional Police detective Jason Sweeting said officers failed to anticipate several factors in their 2020 arrest plan, including Francique's prior victimization. Sweeting testified that Francique walked from his home to his car faster than officers expected, delaying their response. Police had planned to block Francique's vehicle with an unmarked car once he reached it, believing they could arrest him first, according to the inquest. Instead, the operation turned into a high risk takedown after Francique entered his vehicle and put it into motion, the inquest heard. The shooting took place outside a townhouse complex on the evening of Jan. 7, 2020. The inquest also heard there was no urgency to rush the arrest, since Francique had only breached bail conditions days earlier.

items.title: Cedar Tree Circles, Didukh-Making and Mocktail Classes Headline CreativeHub 1352's December Workshop Lineup
items.summary: According to CreativeHub 1352, a new slate of hands-on workshops will run alongside the Mississauga Festival of Trees at the Small Arms Inspection Building from Dec. 4 to 13. The non-profit says the lineup includes an Indigenous Cedar Tree Circle, a session on the Ukrainian tradition of Didukh-making, and a candle-making class. Organizers say other sessions let participants try soft pastels, acrylic painting, needle felting, embroidery and letter writing. CreativeHub 1352 says wellness options are also on offer, including morning yoga, a clarifying face mask workshop and a tasting of Himalayan tartary buckwheat. The group says a mocktail-making class is included too, with proceeds supporting its non-profit programming. CreativeHub 1352 notes free drop-in activities will run throughout the festival for anyone who prefers not to register in advance.

items.title: Santa Claus Parade brings holiday lights and festivities back to Mississauga
items.summary: Santa Claus is coming to Mississauga tomorrow (Nov. 21), bringing a parade of illuminated floats, marching bands and holiday entertainment to downtown streets as the city officially kicks off the Christmas season. , with this year’s theme, “Sauga’s Home for the Holidays,” celebrating the people, cultures, traditions and stories that make up the community. Presented by TD, the free event will also feature the first lighting of the city’s Christmas tree at Celebration Square, as Santa’s sleigh makes its way through the downtown core. m. A DJ dance party, food trucks serving festive treats and photo opportunities with Santa and other holiday characters will be available ahead of the parade. m. m. The parade will feature glowing floats, festive walking groups and marching bands playing holiday favourites. Its theme is intended to reflect the many ways people in Mississauga celebrate the season and come together as a community. The procession will travel through City Centre, with Santa passing through Celebration Square to light the Christmas tree. Motorists should prepare for road closures and parking restrictions in the downtown area beginning at noon Saturday. Several streets will be closed at different times as the parade approaches and passes through the route, with roads reopening once it is safe to do so.

items.title: Local Taxpayers Cover Services Gap as Advocates Say Ontario Shortchanges Peel Non-Profits by $1.4 Billion
items.summary: According to Metamorphosis Network coordinator Sean Meagher, Ontario is underfunding non-profits across Mississauga, Brampton and the wider GTA by roughly $1.4 billion, spanning housing, long-term care and addiction services. Meagher told insauga.com funding outside Toronto has not kept pace with demand, and that the Peel shortfall alone stood at $868 million a year as of 2024. He said Metamorphosis data showed the province gives Peel residents $578 less per person annually than comparable regions, noting Toronto is twice Peel's size yet has six times the affordable housing. Meagher said a gap in one area ripples across the system, with local taxpayers covering costs the province should bear. He added that in York Region, that gap rose by $123 million over the past decade. Meagher said roughly 10 per cent of a resident's tax bill funds services the province should cover.
